data.text:
#WxHistory |
Typhoon Megi '10 (Juan) was a nightmare for the Philippines as it hit Luzon as a C5 super typhoon. Megi was the rare case where US based recon flew into the storm. While the storm's official intensity was 185mph (160kt)/903mb, recon found winds up to 190mph (165kt) & a pressure of 890mb. JMA had a lower pressure of 885mb which became the 9th strongest typhoon on record per JMA. 

Megi's impacts were rather devastating. Storm surge, flooding & extreme winds hammered 🇵🇭, causing numerous deaths & heavy destruction. 

Megi went its way into China. In Taiwan, Megi's outflow contributed major flooding in the island, killing many people in the process.

Megi killed 69-73. While Megi wasn't retired, only the PAGASA name, Juan, was & it was replaced with Jose.

$GRAB "Secret Weapon"📶$500B MC 🧵

Grab Holdings Limited, founded in 2012 as a taxi-hailing service in Malaysia, has transformed into Southeast Asia's leading AI SuperApp, serving over 700 million people across eight countries including Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, and Vietnam. Initially focused on competing with @Uber  in ride-hailing, Grab expanded post its 2018 acquisition of Uber's regional operations, integrating food delivery (GrabFood), grocery delivery (GrabMart), digital payments (GrabPay), financial services (loans, insurance via Grab Financial Group), and recently aggressive tourism expansion with Dine-Out is now the most popular(rank #1) app in SEA. 

This evolution leverages a unified platform where users can access multiple services seamlessly, reducing the need for separate apps and fostering daily reliance. By 2025, AI-driven optimizations, such as personalized recommendations and efficient routing, have further enhanced its ecosystem, with gross merchandise value (GMV) showing consistent double-digit growth in core segments like mobility and deliveries, at 75% market share soon to be 90-95% as $Goto is in decline, Grab is well position to lock in 30-50% average revenue growth for the next 10 years. In addition, the introduction of GrabUnlimited in 2023 marked a pivotal shift, bundling benefits to address post-pandemic economic pressures and solidify user loyalty in an underpenetrated market where only about 6.5% penetration in 700m population, and 14% thesis from Bottom of Pyramid(BOT) core. 

1. So Mike, afte a long intro, what are you talking about? What is the easiest way to understand $Grab "Secret Weapon"

"Affordability", if u want shorter version "A"

Grab's "Secret Weapon" revolves around affordability strategies that deliver tangible value, making the SuperApp indispensable for everyday needs. At the core is GrabUnlimited, a subscription model (typically priced affordably at a monthly fee, with options for annual plans) that replaces unpredictable costs with consistent savings, targeting price-conscious consumers in Southeast Asia's emerging economies. $4.99-$9.99/month is less than 1% for average household income, or less than 2% of individual income. Unlike one-off promotions, it provides a predictable "access pass" to discounts, addressing pain points like high delivery fees that deter frequent usage.

The role of GrabUnlimited:

~Unlimited Discounted Delivery Fees: The flagship "hero benefit" offers reduced or free delivery on GrabFood and GrabMart orders, directly tackling affordability barriers where delivery costs can exceed meal prices

~Mobility Perks: Upgraded in 2025, this now extends savings to rides (e.g., discounts on GrabRide), encouraging cross-service usage from food to transport.

~Basket Discounts and Exclusive Deals: Additional reductions on order totals, plus partner perks like 1-month @OpenAI  GrabGPT Plus access (worth $20), Viu Premium subscriptions for entertainment, and up to 10% off on hotels and flights. 

~Visibility and Trials: Users see real-time savings in their profiles, with free trials (1-3 months) to hook new subscribers amid economic uncertainty. 

These elements create an irreplaceable value proposition that lowers the effective cost of using Grab, making it more accessible for lower-income segments while appealing to frequent users. Broader affordability initiatives include ecosystem lending ( GXS Bank), carpooling options like GrabShare, and AI-enhanced efficiencies that reduce operational costs passed to users.This strategy has driven record monthly transacting users (MTUs) to 34.9m by mid-2023, now at 46m MTUs as of Q2 2025. Competition has weakened since. 

@AnthonyPY_Tan understood, nonstop price war was unsustainable. Affordability is still central, but without superior value proposition, there will be no differentiation!

2. How Affordability Drives Value and User Stickiness

GrabUnlimited's affordability focus creates stickiness by embedding habitual use through perceived value, leading to higher engagement, retention, and spending. Subscribers benefit from cost predictabilitysuch as  avoiding surging delivery fees, which builds trust and reduces churn. 

Key data:

Food Delieveries: 5x higher in Q2 2025, encourages frequent orders, contributing over 1/3 of Deliveries GMV

Retention rates: 2x higher in 6 months, nearly half GrabUnlimited chose 12 months plans. This reduces churn by locking in long-term commitment via value.

Unlock users to multi-service usage as Grab SuperApp is not just a business, but a relationship where SEA consumers can trust, reliable! Over 70% use multiple Grab Services, strengthens ecosystem stickiness. 

Overall statistic: 50% of top spenders are GrabUnlimited users, this will lead to cross-sell to mobility/financial/tourism/dine-out.

3. Grab "Secret Weapon" approach is similar to @amazon Prime Model (No I'm saying $GRAB is the next $AMZN)

Context: As of July 2025, an estimated 197 million Amazon Prime members were in the US or 57% penetration, where $GRAB is a much younger company, if executed properly, that is $2B-$4B/m subscription to net income at 14% thesis, or $14-$20B at 100% thesis Bottom of Pyramid.

Grab's approach mirrors Amazon's ecosystem stickiness, where Prime membership builds trust through reliable, value-driven services like fast shipping, easy returns, and customer support, encouraging users to default to the platform for most needs. Both rely on subscription models to create "shallow switching costs" that evolve into deep loyalty. 

~Value Through Core Perks: Amazon Prime's free 2-day shipping reduces friction in e-commerce, much like GrabUnlimited's discounted deliveries eliminate barriers in food and mobility, associating the brand with affordability and convenience

~Trust and Reliability: Amazon users trust the brand for seamless returns and service, fostering repeat business; similarly, Grab builds trust via consistent savings, priority support in VIP tiers, and AI-enhanced reliability (better driver matching), leading to higher lifetime value. 

~Ecosystem Lock-In: Prime extends to video streaming and groceries, increasing cross-usage; GrabUnlimited bundles rides, deliveries, and external perks (ChatGPT), driving multi-service adoption and making the app "sticky" for daily life.

~Data-Driven Retention: Both use subscriptions to gather user data for personalization, with Amazon's resulting in higher spend (Prime members spend ~2x more annually) paralleling Grab's 4-5x uplift. The reason Grab retention is much higher due to "Secret Sauce" that treating Users/Merchants/Drivers as customers. These Merchants/Drivers are also Grab loyal customers.  

4. So "Affordability" is core to $GRAB SuperApp, how the company going to expand margin to help Long Term shareholders?

Adding more High-Margin products/users and Initiatives

~Enterprise Saas and Advanced Booking Tools: Rolled out in Q2 2025, these B2B offerings (e.g., API integrations for fleet management and corporate travel booking) yield 60-80% margins due to one-time setup fees and recurring subscriptions. They contributed $20M+ in new revenue, with uptake from 500+ enterprises, boosting Others segment margins to +15%

~Insurance and Wealth Products: Expanded via GrabInsure, with micro-insurance bundled into Unlimited ( ride protection at $0.50/trip). Premiums grew 50% YoY to $150M annualized, at 70% margins, as claims ratios dropped to 45% with data-driven personalization.

~Advertising Monetization in Fintech: New in-app ad slots for financial products ( loan pre-approvals) drove 60% YoY ad revenue growth to $176M in Q1, with Fintech-specific ads adding 20 bps to margins.

~AI-Enhanced Lending Models: Q2 pilots using predictive analytics for SME loans reduced default rates by 15%, enabling 10% higher pricing power and +200 bps NIM lift. Loan disbursements hit $721M in Q2 (+44% YoY), with >$1B targeted by YE2025. 

~Tourism expansion with @Alipay (1.7B users) and @KlookTravel (50m MAUs) with flexiable payment options. Tourists are 70% more likely to book premium services for faster booking, and relatively cheap to their income. This segment is 152m visitors in 2025, and projected to 250m in 2030. 20-30% of this market share will translate to $10B+ revenue at 30-50% contribution margin over the long term. Tourism Expansion is low risk-high reward initiative. 

~Dine-Out: This is one of the highest margin segment with (20-35% commission with Margin up to 80%). @AnthonyPY_Tan learnt it well from @Groupon , to give merchants/restaurants flexible deal structure(group deal), and help the businesses to get more visibility. Restaurants have reported 300-400% surge in traffic after using Dine-Out. Early data suggested 1/3 of new users are Dine-Out hunters. This again enhances $GRAB SuperApp "Secret Weapon". 
The best part? Nearly 2 million restaurants in SEA want to buy visibility, this is such a massive market that could bring in $5B+ a year on revenue with massive contribution to EPS. And don't forget these restaurants are likely to spend on GrabAds to gain even more exposure! This could easily flywheel to $10B+ a year revenue.

~Drone/Autonomous: Mobility/Delivery still dominate most of Grab Revenue, @AnthonyPY_Tan knows that margin has to improve over the long term by integrating AI-driven autonomy, Grab aims to slash variable costs ( driver wages, fuel) and achieve software-like margins (40-60%) in scaled operations, similar to how Amazon's drone pilots have reduced last-mile expenses by up to 50% in test markets. Below, I outline the key 2025 developments, their mechanics, and margin implications, drawing from pilots in Singapore and the Philippines.

Conclusion:  Under the bold leadership of CEO @AnthonyPY_Tan, has transformed from a regional ride-hailing pioneer into Southeast Asia’s leading superapp, poised to lock in 30-50% average revenue growth over the next 5-10 years. By October 2025, Grab’s strategic affordability-driven user stickiness via GrabUnlimited, high-margin Financial Services expansion,Tourism, Dine-Out and cutting-edge autonomous and drone technologies creates a powerful flywheel that mirrors Amazon’s ecosystem dominance while addressing SEA’s unique economic and urban challenges. This convergence, rooted in Tan’s vision to make Grab the “everyday everything app,” positions the company to capitalize on a $1 Trillion+ digital economy, delivering unparalleled value to its 46M+ monthly transacting users (MTUs) and cementing its market leadership at 75% market share and soon to be 90-95%.

GrabUnlimited, with its low-cost subscription model offering discounted deliveries, rides, and exclusive perks (ChatGPT Plus, Viu Premium), has redefined affordability in SEA’s price-sensitive markets. By slashing delivery fees and bundling multi-service savings, it drives 4-5x higher spending and 4x order frequency among subscribers, who contribute over one-third of Deliveries GMV and exhibit 2x retention rates. This mirrors Amazon Prime’s trust-building through reliable shipping and returns, embedding Grab into daily routines. 

Anthony with work ethic “You can sleep all you want when you're dead” wants to dominate long term, my capital shall be betting on this horse, to be part of uplift 5 billion people out of POVERTY with pure Capitalism, not Socialism!
